thread:
emily: Heads up - FinServX POC kickoff. They want Redwood Private deployed into a customer VPC (onprem -> cloud tunnel) with two hard requirements: 1) preserve original client IP for their audit pipeline, 2) very strict egress (deny-by-default). They prefer minimal changes to their network team. Can we sketch options and an example firewall allowlist?

rahul: Short answer: there are 3 realistic patterns we recommend: PrivateLink (interface endpoint), VPC Peering (or cross-account peering), or TGW/DirectConnect. Tradeoffs: PrivateLink = simplest to approve (no routing changes) but ENI SNAT will replace src IP; Peering/TGW = preserves 5-tuple end-to-end but needs routing & possibly peering approvals.

emily: They asked if we can do Proxy Protocol or preserve X-Forwarded-For so their SIEM can see original client IPs even if packet src is the endpoint. Is Proxy Protocol an option?

tom: Proxy Protocol can work if we control an L4 load balancer that speaks it. Options:
- Run an NLB in front of our service that supports Proxy Protocol v2 -> then app must accept proxy-protocol header. This preserves original IP at app layer but still requires active config.
- Use application-layer X-Forwarded-For from our reverse proxy -> easiest, works over HTTPS, signed headers can satisfy audit checks.
- For true TCP-level preservation (no headers), use VPC Peering or TGW so source IPs traverse end-to-end.

nina: Note: PrivateLink traffic appears to come from the endpoint ENI IP. If FinServX's compliance team requires the network layer to contain original src, PrivateLink won't pass. But many auditors accept header-based attribution if you provide a cryptographic signing mechanism + chain-of-custody note. We have template language for that.

rahul: Example decision matrix we usually send:
- PrivateLink: Pros = fastest security sign-off, minimal route changes, works with SNI/TLS inspect. Cons = NATs source IPs, potential extra hop for latency.
- VPC Peering: Pros = preserves src IPs, lower egress cost in-region, lower latency. Cons = requires peering approvals, cross-account routes, scaling considerations (routes per prefix).
- Transit Gateway (TGW) + DirectConnect/VPN: Pros = best control for multi-spoke, onprem -> cloud stable path, preserves IPs. Cons = higher setup time + infra cost.

emily: They also want a concrete firewall snippet their netsec team can paste. Can someone draft a minimal, conservative allowlist (FQDN + CIDR fallback) we can provide?

tom: Draft allowlist (pasteable):
```
# Minimal outbound from corporate firewall/proxy to Redwood PrivateDeploy
# Prefer FQDN allowlist configured on corporate proxy
ALLOW tcp 443 to private.redwood-inference.net (TLS)  # control plane & API calls
ALLOW tcp 443 to models-download.redwood-inference.net  # model pulls (optional, can be restricted by maintenance windows)
# Optional telemetry/metrics endpoints
ALLOW tcp 443 to telemetry.redwood-inference.net
# If using CIDR (customer insists): Allow outbound to 198.51.100.0/22 and 203.0.113.0/24 (example stable ranges) - we will provide final CIDRs and change window commitments.
# For VPN/DirectConnect: Allow IPsec ports to our VPN termination IPs (we will share during onboarding).
```
Caveat: If they maintain strict egress by CIDR, we need a scheduled change window for updates. We prefer FQDNs when corporate proxies are in use.

nina: Add note about TLS inspection: If FinServX TLS-inspects outbound, SNI might be rewritten; recommend they allow TLS passthrough to our FQDN or add our cert CN to inspection exception so SNI reaches the endpoint. Otherwise PrivateLink + SNI-inspect can break routing to the correct endpoint.

rahul: Cost quick-numbers, non-binding: for ~5TB/month egress (in-region):
- PrivateLink: endpoint-hour + data processing. Rough ballpark $0.02-$0.06/GB depending on cloud and region. Predictable but slightly higher at this scale.
- Peering/TGW: lower per-GB ($0.005-$0.03/GB typical) but you bear connectivity costs (DirectConnect or VPN).
Summary: If they're price-sensitive at 5TB/mo, peering/TGW likely wins; if they need fast security sign-off, PrivateLink wins.

emily: Security questionnaire: they asked for language about "how client identity is preserved". Can we give a short paragraph they can paste?

nina: Pasteable snippet: "When traffic traverses a PrivateLink interface endpoint, the endpoint ENI becomes the source IP for our service. To preserve client identity at the application level we emit authenticated X-Forwarded-For headers and optionally support Proxy Protocol v2 on TCP. For customers requiring network-layer source IP preservation, we recommend cross-account VPC Peering or a Transit Gateway-based topology. We can provide a signed header workflow and audit-ready logs as part of the PrivateDeploy runbook."

tom: infra-bot: :white_check_mark: sandbox-finservx provisioned in eu-west-1. Shared drive: https://drive.redwood/finservx-poc-setup (creds in secret manager).

emily: Nice. Action items: rahul will draft the 1-page decision table + cost example. nina will produce the firewall snippet + the questionnaire language and a short paragraph about TLS inspection. tom will add an NLB + proxy-protocol checklist in case they go that route. Aim to send to customer in 24h.

rahul: On it. I'll also include expected CIDR lists and a proposed maintenance window for IP rotations.

emily: Thanks team. I'll schedule the customer sync after we have the doc. :thumbsup:
